deck: MATCH EACH BORROWER TO THE ONE LENDER WHOSE CREDIT BOX FITS, PACKAGE A CLEAN FILE, AND GET PAID ONLY WHEN IT FUNDS
PRICE POINTS, PACKAGING DEPOSITS, BACK-END SPLITS, AND FACTORING RESIDUALS ACROSS EQUIPMENT, FACTORING, ABL, SBA, MCA, DSCR, AND CAPITAL STACKS
site_ui.lead: Practitioners show how a commercial loan broker who never lends a dollar of their own money turns bank declines into funded deals, from $30,000 on a $2 million loan at 1.5 points to factoring residuals of 10% to 15% of monthly factor fees.
site_ui.summary: All 12 chapters synthesize 192 verbatim YouTube practitioner testimonies, with every quote, metric, pro-tip, and operator gate carrying timestamped inline attribution to its source video. The chapters cover the full brokerage path, from deal economics and launching a brokerage through equipment finance, factoring, SBA lending, merchant cash advances, DSCR underwriting, and capital stacks.

flow: Score the file on deal size, deal type, borrower constraints, and time pressure, and check that the prospect's story matches the bank statements and balance sheet before quoting points.
Run LTV, DSCR, and debt yield yourself from the rent roll, P&L, and PFS, because a 10% debt yield against an 11% lender test opens a funding gap.
Call bank commercial managers on Monday or Tuesday to ask where the money is going this week, then place the file with one lender whose credit box fits instead of spraying it.
Take a packaging deposit, even $250 with a 45-day LOI refund clause, and set the hair clause up front so messy deals add points at the end.
Scrub the package for credit reports older than 60 days, inactive LLCs, and missing pages, and answer every borrower and referral within 24 to 48 hours.
Get paid only when the deal funds, then work the capital stack for repeat financing events across acquisition, rehab, permanent financing, equipment, and working capital.
